newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO likely to recommend new command in Spain.
newsitem.headline: NATO likely to recommend new command in Spain.

text.p: NATO military officials, following Spain's decision to join the alliance's military structure, are expected to recommend next week the creation of a new sub-regional command centre on Spanish territory.
A senior military official said on Friday that military chiefs of staff from the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation would make the recommendation at a meeting on November 21-22 in Brussels.
The Spanish Parliament voted on Thursday to endorse government plans for Spain to become fully integrated into NATO's military structure.
NATO currently has three regional commands in Europe -- in Britain, the Netherlands and Italy -- and sub-regional commands scattered across the continent.
An issue yet to be decided regarding the Spanish command is whether it will include the Canary Islands, the Spanish archepelago in the Atlantic.

They are currently the responsibility of NATO's Atlantic command, rather than its European command. Spain has insisted that the islands be treated as national territory and wants them to be part of the new sub-region.
